subject: business-studies
topicDisplay: Operations Finance And Influences On Business
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Reducing a business's environmental impact might involve:
options: Recycling, cutting waste and using renewable energy
questions.explain: Businesses reduce environmental impact through recycling, cutting waste and using cleaner energy.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of using technology such as automation in operations?
options: It removes the need for any quality control
It can increase productivity and consistency
questions.explain: Automation can raise productivity and produce more consistent output, though it has set-up costs.

questions.q: Stakeholders such as the local community might pressure a business to:
options: Reduce noise and pollution from its operations
questions.explain: Local communities are stakeholders who may pressure a business to limit pollution, noise and other local harms.

questions.q: Employment law includes rules about:
options: Minimum wage, discrimination and working conditions
questions.explain: Employment law covers areas such as the minimum wage, anti-discrimination and safe working conditions.

questions.q: What is the difference between quality control and quality assurance?
options: Quality control checks products at the end; quality assurance builds quality into the whole process
Quality control happens only after sale
questions.explain: Quality control inspects finished goods, while quality assurance builds quality in at every stage.

questions.q: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
options: Profit is always paid in cash immediately
Profit and cash are the same thing
Customers may pay later while the business must pay its own bills now
questions.explain: Profit and cash differ in timing; a firm can be profitable yet short of cash if money comes in slowly.

questions.q: One advantage of globalisation for a UK consumer is:
options: A wider choice of products, often at lower prices
questions.explain: Globalisation gives consumers a wider choice of goods from around the world, often at competitive prices.

questions.q: If interest rates fall, the most likely effect is that:
options: Borrowing and consumer spending tend to increase
questions.explain: Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper, which tends to encourage borrowing, investment and consumer spending.

questions.q: During a recession (a downturn in the business cycle), businesses often experience:
questions.explain: In a recession consumer spending falls, so many businesses see lower demand and sales.

questions.q: Variable costs are costs that:
options: Change directly with the level of output
Are paid only once a year
Stay the same whatever the output
questions.explain: Variable costs (e.g. raw materials) rise and fall with the amount produced.

questions.q: Which of the following is total revenue?
options: Selling price multiplied by quantity sold
questions.explain: Total revenue = selling price x quantity sold.

questions.q: What is a drawback of holding too much stock (overstocking)?
options: Money tied up in stock and higher storage and waste costs
questions.explain: Holding excess stock ties up cash and increases storage, insurance and potential wastage costs.

questions.q: If the exchange rate of the pound rises (strong pound), UK exports tend to become:
questions.explain: A stronger pound makes UK exports more expensive for overseas buyers, which can reduce export demand.

questions.q: Efficiency in operations means:
options: Producing output using the fewest resources and least waste
Always producing the cheapest possible product
Hiring as many workers as possible
questions.explain: Efficiency means getting the most output from the available inputs while minimising waste.

questions.q: On a break-even chart, the break-even point is shown where:
options: The revenue line reaches its highest point
The total revenue line crosses the total costs line
questions.explain: Break-even occurs where the total revenue line crosses the total costs line, so revenue exactly covers costs.

questions.q: What is productivity?
options: The total amount of stock held
Output produced per unit of input (e.g. per worker) in a given time
questions.explain: Productivity measures output per input, such as the number of units produced per worker per hour.

questions.q: Economies of scale lead to:
options: A fall in average cost per unit as output increases
A rise in average cost per unit as output increases
questions.explain: Economies of scale mean the average cost per unit falls as a business produces on a larger scale.

questions.q: A key feature of lean production is to:
options: Increase the number of defective products
Minimise waste of all kinds while maintaining quality
Hold as much stock as possible
questions.explain: Lean production focuses on cutting waste (time, materials, stock) while keeping quality high.

questions.q: A trade-off between ethics and profit occurs when:
options: Ethics and profit always rise together
Doing the most ethical thing reduces profit, forcing a choice
questions.explain: A trade-off means choosing the more ethical option may lower profit, so the business must balance the two.

questions.q: A reliable supplier is important to a business mainly because it helps to ensure:
options: Materials of the right quality arrive on time so production is not disrupted
questions.explain: A dependable supplier delivers the right quality on time, keeping production running smoothly.

questions.q: Net profit margin is calculated as:
questions.explain: Net profit margin = (net profit divided by revenue) x 100, expressed as a percentage.

questions.q: Procurement in operations refers to:
options: Sourcing and buying the materials and supplies a business needs
questions.explain: Procurement is the process of finding suppliers and purchasing the inputs a business needs.
